title: Amid railway crisis after Mangaluru's exit from Palakkad division, experts urge this solution
content: Following the separation of the Mangaluru section from the Palakkad division, Kerala must immediately demand a special compensation package from the Railway Board to offset the severe losses. Retired railway officials and experts warn that the state must act swiftly to approve and construct a new terminal station at Kumbla in Kasaragod within three months, a project that is expected to take at least two years to complete. The urgent need for a terminal at Kumbla To mitigate the impact of losing Mangaluru, state MPs must proactively spearhead the Kumbla terminal proposal. According to former railway officials, the first phase of development at Kumbla must prioritise the construction of two maintenance pit lines, four platforms, and two stabling lines. If the state government can successfully acquire and hand over more land, the terminal can be further expanded in the second phase. Without a dedicated terminal of its own, running domestic trains efficiently within Kerala will become practically impossible. Operational hurdles and loss of autonomy In the past, the Southern Railway zone could operate trains to Mangaluru without external approvals. However, following the administrative shake-up, Kerala-bound trains will now require clearance from the South Western Railway zone for every single run, with no guarantee of smooth approvals. Alarmingly, local interest groups in Karnataka are already demanding that Kerala-bound services be shifted from Mangaluru Central to Mangaluru Junction to reserve the premier central station exclusively for Karnataka's internal services. A call for political unity The bifurcation of the Palakkad division was the result of a coordinated, persistent campaign by MPs from southern Karnataka. Because this was largely a political decision, Kerala—which lacks equivalent political leverage at the centre—struggled to mount an effective defence. Railway experts warn that if Kerala's MPs do not look beyond basic demands for individual train stops and fail to present a united front, the state risks losing the Parasala to Kanyakumari stretch next, which is currently sought after by the Madurai division. Historically, the Palakkad division spent crores of rupees developing the railway stations and infrastructure in Mangaluru. Yet, because successive administrations neglected to build similar facilities in Kasaragod, Kozhikode, or Kannur, Palakkad has now been left as a major railway division without a single terminal of its own.
